skill.name: url-citation-search
skill.description: Find papers and preprints that cite a URL, with evidence from references, PDFs, HTML, DOI links, arXiv, or BibTeX.
skill.summary: Find papers and preprints that cite web pages, with evidence from references, PDFs, or HTML.
skill.author: zjsxply

security_audit.summary: All nine static findings are false positives caused by inline Markdown backticks around terms such as URL variants and source names. I found no prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or executable command instructions in SKILL.md.

static_findings.snippet: - Keep obvious variants: `http/https`, `www/non-www`, trailing slash, moved domains, and mirrored or
- Keep direct-URL variants separate from mirror URLs. The final report should distinguish `direct ci
- Site-restricted searches on academic sources such as `arxiv.org`, `openreview.net`, `aclanthology.
- Publisher article pages may expose references in HTML metadata such as `citation_reference` or ded
- arXiv HTML bibliography entries may hide the real target inside `External Links` even when the vis
- Keep official same-site variants separate from mirrors. Examples: `/engineering/...` versus `/rese
- Separate `confirmed` from `candidate` when verification is incomplete.
- When useful, distinguish `direct`, `official variant`, and `mirror` citation.
- Standard citation indexes often miss web pages, so reverse search on URL, title, and slug is usual

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 19 uses Markdown inline code to name URL variants such as http, https, and www. It does not instruct the model to execute a command or run user input.
Line 20 uses inline code formatting for report labels like direct citation and mirror citation. These are output categories, not shell commands.
Line 33 lists academic website domains inside Markdown backticks for search targeting. There is no command execution syntax or instruction to invoke a shell.
Line 41 names citation_reference as an HTML metadata field using inline code formatting. This is a data field reference, not executable code.
Line 42 formats External Links as a label to inspect in arXiv HTML. It directs verification of href targets and does not request command execution.
Line 49 uses inline code for URL path examples such as /engineering and /research. These are literal paths for citation matching, not shell commands.
Line 50 formats confirmed and candidate as status labels. No external command, interpreter, or executable instruction is present.
Line 58 uses inline code for citation-type labels in the final report. The labels do not create a command injection or shell execution path.
Line 63 uses inline code for the cited by phrase as a search-index concept. It is explanatory Markdown text, not executable code.

content.value_statement: Web pages are often cited in papers but missed by standard citation indexes. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to verify URL citations with direct evidence.
actual_capabilities: Builds search keys from full URLs, host paths, page titles, and slugs.
Searches academic sources, publisher pages, preprints, and general web results.
Verifies citations through PDF text, HTML references, metadata, or bibliography links.
Distinguishes direct citations, official URL variants, and mirror citations.
Deduplicates preprints and published versions while preserving access fallbacks.
Can produce brief lists, citation reports, or BibTeX when requested.
limitations: Requires web access or provided search results to find citing works.
Cannot prove absence of citations across every closed or private database.
PDF extraction may miss references when text or link annotations are unavailable.
Search quality depends on the target page title, URL stability, and available metadata.

use_cases.title: Track Blog Impact
use_cases.description: Find papers that cite a technical blog post and separate confirmed citations from loose topic matches.

use_cases.title: Audit Project Citations
use_cases.description: Check whether academic papers cite a project page, documentation page, or migrated official URL.

use_cases.title: Build Evidence Reports
use_cases.description: Create a concise citation report with links, evidence notes, DOI details, and preprint fallbacks.

prompt_templates.title: Find Confirmed Citations
prompt_templates.prompt: Use url-citation-search to find papers that cite this URL: [URL]. Return only confirmed citations with evidence notes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner search for one web page.

prompt_templates.title: Check Official Variants
prompt_templates.prompt: Use url-citation-search for [URL]. Include direct citations, official URL variants, and mirrors in separate groups.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate search where the target page may have moved.

prompt_templates.title: Produce BibTeX
prompt_templates.prompt: Use url-citation-search for [URL]. Verify each citing work, then return BibTeX for confirmed citing papers.

prompt_templates.title: Create Audit Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Use url-citation-search for [URL]. Search title, slug, mirrors, arXiv, OpenReview, ACM, IEEE, and publisher references. Explain rejected candidates.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced evidence audit for a difficult URL.

output_examples.input: Find papers that cite a machine learning blog post URL.
output_examples.output: Confirmed citations grouped by direct URL, official variant, and mirror. Each entry includes title, year, link, and evidence note.

output_examples.input: Check whether a project page is cited in arXiv papers.
output_examples.output: A short report listing verified arXiv papers, matched reference text, and candidates rejected because no visible citation was found.

output_examples.input: Return BibTeX for papers that cite this documentation page.
output_examples.output: BibTeX entries for confirmed citing works, plus a note describing how each citation was verified.

best_practices: Provide the exact target URL and any known old domains or mirrors.
Ask for confirmed citations when you need evidence suitable for reporting.
Request BibTeX only after candidate works have been verified.
anti_patterns: Do not treat search snippets as proof of citation.
Do not merge mirror citations with direct citations when provenance matters.
Do not assume a published paper preserves a citation found in its preprint.

faq.question: Can this find citations to any web page?
faq.answer: It can guide searches for public citations, but it cannot guarantee coverage of closed databases or inaccessible documents.

faq.question: Does it require a DOI for the target page?
faq.answer: No. It is designed for URLs, blogs, documentation pages, project pages, and other web content.

faq.question: How does it verify a citation?
faq.answer: It checks PDF text, HTML references, metadata, bibliography pages, or underlying links for the target URL or verified variants.

faq.question: Can it return BibTeX?
faq.answer: Yes. It can return BibTeX for confirmed citing papers when the user requests bibliography output.

faq.question: Will it count topic matches as citations?
faq.answer: No. A work must expose the target URL, title, slug, or verified mirror in citation evidence.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
